test_title: SSC CGL Tier 2 Quant Previous Year Paper (Held On: 3 Feb 2022)
subject: general
question: Two pillars A and B of the same height are on opposite sides of a road which is 40 m wide. The angles of elevation of the tops of the pillars A and B are 30° and 45°, respectively, at a point on the road between the pillars. What is the distance (in m) of the point from the foot of pillar A?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Height is same for both pillars, so use ratio method.

For 30°, height : base = 1 : √3. For 45°, height : base = 1 : 1.

Total road width = Sum of bases = (√3 + 1) units.

Given √3 + 1 units = 40 m ⇒ 1 unit = 40 / (√3 + 1) m.

Distance from A (base of 30°) = √3 units = 40√3 / (√3 + 1) m.

Rationalizing: 40√3(√3 − 1) ÷ (3 − 1) = 20(3 − √3) m.

**∴ The correct answer is 20(3−√3) m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Width of road = 40 m

Height of pillar A = Height of pillar B = h

Angle of elevation of A = 30°

Angle of elevation of B = 45°

**Formula Used:**

tan θ = Height / Base

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b3acbc4d4d48c245fe8efec86e47ff6b3797df96f0e1d1d93459fe159abbb47d.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the distance of the point P from pillar A (A') be x m.

Then, the distance of the point P from pillar B (B') = (40 − x) m.

In ΔAA'P:

⇒ tan 30° = h / x

⇒ 1 / √3 = h / x

⇒ h = x / √3 ---- (1)

In ΔBB'P:

⇒ tan 45° = h / (40 − x)

⇒ 1 = h / (40 − x)

⇒ h = 40 − x ---- (2)

Equating (1) and (2):

⇒ x / √3 = 40 − x

⇒ x = 40√3 − x√3

⇒ x(1 + √3) = 40√3

⇒ x = 40√3 / (√3 + 1)

⇒ x = [40√3 / (√3 + 1)] × [(√3 − 1) / (√3 − 1)]

⇒ x = [40√3(√3 − 1)] / (3 − 1)

⇒ x = [40(3 − √3)] / 2

⇒ x = 20(3 − √3) m

**∴ The correct answer is 20(3−√3) m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Standard Trigonometric Ratios

For height and distance, remember tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, and tan 60° = √3.

Rationalization of Denominator

To simplify fractions with surds like a / (√b + c), multiply both numerator and denominator by the conjugate (√b − c).

Angle of Elevation

The angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when looking up at an object. It equals the angle of depression from the object to the point.</p
